newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says doesn't rule out more funds for bad loans.
newsitem.headline: MOF says doesn't rule out more funds for bad loans.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said it would not rule out the use of fresh public money to tackle the problem of bad loans faced by private financial institutions.

Asked whether the MOF had any plans to use fresh public funds to deal with the bad loan issue, a senior MOF official said: "We intend to tackle the bad loan issue taking into account the conditions at the time."

The official, answering a question at a parliamentary committee, said that MOF's stance on the issue was that no further public money should be used for bad loans held at non-bank financial institutions other than those at the failed "jusen" mortgage firms.
The government last year budgeted 685 billion yen in tax money to help wind up failed mortgage firms.

The issue of pitching in tax money has recently come into the spotlight again after an opposition politician made a call to reopen debate on the issue, followed by supportive comments by key members of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party.
Although Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka had ruled out the use of fresh public funds at a news conference on Tuesday, he chose not to do so today at a parliamentary committee meeting.
Asked the same question, Mitsuzuka only said he shared the view expressed by the ministry official.
